messages:
Alex K: heads-up — we just got a support escalation from AcmeCorp: sudden 429s for batch inference started ~10m ago. they say it affected a handful of endpoints and caused timeouts in their job worker. :rotating_light:
Maya P: on it. any alert fired?
OncallBot: ALERT: limiter_high_429_rate for service=hosted-api region=us-west triggered at 1979991070 — 70% 429 rate over 1m. pager duty escalated to eng-sre oncall.
Jamie (support): repro steps from customer: run 10 concurrent streaming sessions, ~50 rps each, after ~30s they start getting 429s. they included a sample curl + stream snippet. said they didn't change client.
Ingrid S: can you paste the curl?
Jamie (support): sure —
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v2","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}' \
  --parallel --repeat 10
```
They also attached latency graphs from their side — p50 stayed fine, p95 spiked then 429s.
Ravi N: checking limiter config. there was a config rollout 4h ago that changed per-tenant burst_window from 1s to 250ms to improve fairness. could that explain it?
Alex K: interesting — customer used long-lived streaming connections, so aggressive micro-windowing could cause many small windows to exhaust token buckets quickly.
Ingrid S: pulling limiter metrics for the tenant_id they provided — tenant: acmecorp-42.
DeployBot: deploy rlim-config-v3 promoted to prod by maya-p at 1979988000 (config id rlim-v3).
Ingrid S: metrics: acmecorp-42 saw a spike in reject_count starting 1979991000, reject rate peaked at 78% for streaming route `/v1/stream`. global reject_count also up but concentrated on a few tenants.
Maya P: do we have tokenbucket refill unit mismatch? previous incidents had refill unit in ms vs seconds. check the config keys.
Ravi N: config diff — prior `burst_window_ms: 1000` now `burst_window_ms: 250`. also `refill_amount` unchanged. code expects burst_window in ms. nothing else looks off.
Alex K: that is a legit change. for streaming workloads, reducing the window to 250ms increases effective rate limit checks by 4x, which can surface rejections if clients have uneven token consumption.
Jamie (support): customer insists they didn't change anything on their side and just got worse after 12:00. their incident start aligns with our deploy timestamp.
Luis T: product note — we intentionally tightened windows to reduce multi-tenant hogging. but we didn't anticipate long-lived streaming semantics.
Ingrid S: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback the rlim-config-v3 (restore burst_window_ms=1000) 2) whitelist acmecorp-42 to use rlim-v2 via temporary routing 3) bump per-tenant burst tokens for streaming routes.
Alex K: rollback seems fastest. but let's also add a safety: when a tenant has active streaming connections, use a different limiter policy that counts per-connection instead of per-request. long-term fix.
Maya P: agree. initiating rollback now.
DeployBot: rollback started for config rlim-v3 -> rlim-v2 (requested by maya-p).
OncallBot: NOTE: Scheduled config rollback at 1979991325.
Ravi N: I'm watching the limiter metrics. rolling back now.
Ingrid S: logs from limiter for acmecorp-42 around 1979991040:
```
WARN limiter: tenant=acmecorp-42 route=/v1/stream tokenbucket_exhausted window_ms=250 remaining=0
DEBUG limiter: consumed=512 tokens req_id=abc123 conn_id=stream-57
```
Those debug lines show fairly large token consumption per request — streaming flushes.
Alex K: rollback complete?
DeployBot: rollback complete at 1979991360. rlim-v2 active.
Ingrid S: reject_rate dropping — acmecorp-42 rejects down to 3% within 40s. customer confirms errors cleared.
Jamie (support): customer says their jobs retried and completed, thanks. they asked for a root-cause explanation and permanent workaround.
Luis T: short RCA: config change reduced burst_window to 250ms to curb fairness but unintentionally penalized long-lived streaming connections because of finer-grained windowing combined with per-request token accounting.
Maya P: action items: (1) revert config change permanently until we have streaming-aware policy (2) implement policy flag `streaming_mode` that uses per-connection accounting (3) add automated canary for limiter config changes targeting high-streaming tenants (4) improve rollout notes and include example workloads.
Ravi N: I'll sketch `streaming_mode` design — per-connection token buckets with periodic refill scaled to connection duration. will include metrics to detect regressions.
Ingrid S: also adding an alert that fires when a config rollout coincides with >50% of 429s from <5 tenants. that would've flagged the pattern faster.
Alex K: thanks all. Jamie, please send the customer a summary and offer a dedicated sync to walk through mitigation. also CC SRE on the update.
Jamie (support): will do. sending summary now and scheduling a 1:1. :thumbsup:
Luis T: long-term: consider adding a simulation harness to run common customer patterns (parallel streaming, batch jobs) against config changes in staging before prod rollout.
Ravi N: noted. I'll open a PR for streaming_mode design and add tests.
Ingrid S: post-incident: creating a short postmortem doc and linking to this thread.
Alex K: nice triage — closing thread once postmortem links are in.
OncallBot: Incident resolved at 1979991400.
